name: MongoDB
model: Collections of JSON-like (BSON) documents with nested fields and arrays; rich query language, secondary indexes, aggregation pipelines
engine_note: WiredTiger storage engine: B-trees with document-level concurrency, compression and a journal (write-ahead log)
consistency: Single-document writes are atomic; multi-document transactions (snapshot isolation) are an option. Default write concern is majority (since 5.0) but default read concern is local. Reads from secondaries can be stale.

jepsen.finding: With default and even stronger write settings, partitions lost a large share of acknowledged writes (up to about 42% in one run).
Even 'strictly consistent' reads could see stale data and writes that were later rolled back; fixed later by linearizable read concern and protocol v1.
Replication protocol v0 can lose majority-committed writes by design; v1 bugs were fixed in 3.2.12/3.4.0, which then passed with majority writes and linearizable reads.
Causal consistency sessions only hold with majority reads and writes; with the then-default weaker levels they broke, which MongoDB documented rather than changed.
Transactions did not give snapshot isolation even at strong settings (they ignored collection-level concerns and defaulted weak); a retry bug was fixed in 4.2.8, weak defaults were documented.

scaling: Replica sets for failover and read replicas; built-in sharding splits collections by a shard key you choose, with automatic balancing (resharding possible).

licence_events.event: MongoDB Community Server moves from GNU AGPLv3 to SSPLv1 for all releases and patches from this date

managed: MongoDB Atlas (on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure)
Compatible APIs, not MongoDB: Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB, Amazon DocumentDB
version_note: 9.0.0, 9.0.1 and 9.0.2 are all dated 2026-09-28 in the release notes; GitHub had only r9.0.0-alpha tags when checked. Previous series 8.3 (r8.3.11, 2026-09-11) and 8.0.
reach: Reach for it when records are naturally nested documents whose shape varies, read and written whole, and you want built-in sharding and a managed service.
avoid: Avoid when your data is highly relational with many joins and cross-record invariants, or when the SSPL licence is a problem for your product.
escape: Your records are nested documents of varying shape and you want sharding built in.
chat: Could hold a whole chat with its messages as one document, though Postgres JSONB covers this for most apps.
notes: MongoDB 9.0 became GA on 2026-09-28 per its release notes (three patch numbers share that date; 9.0.3 listed as upcoming). Default write concern is w:majority except in some arbiter setups where it falls back to w:1. Versions for the 2013 and 2015 aphyr posts are the ones named in the post text (2.4.3; 2.6.7). aphyr.com is blocked from this network (HTTP 451), dates read from Wayback Machine copies. SSPL is not OSI-approved.
